skill.name: data-engineer
skill.description: Guide the design of scalable pipelines, warehouses, lakehouses, quality controls, governance, and cloud data platforms using modern data tools.
skill.summary: Plan reliable batch, streaming, warehouse, lakehouse, quality, and governance solutions across modern cloud data stacks.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The sole static finding is a false positive caused by a list of real-time analytics products in SKILL.md. No system reconnaissance instructions, prompt injection, or other malicious intent were found.

static_findings.snippet: - Real-time analytics with Apache Pinot, ClickHouse, Apache Druid

finding_verdicts.reason: Lines 45-46 only list real-time analytics and OLAP technologies. They contain no instruction to inspect a host, collect system details, or execute reconnaissance.

content.value_statement: Data teams need reliable architectures that meet scale, latency, governance, and cost requirements. This skill turns those requirements into pipeline designs, implementation plans, quality controls, and operating guidance.
actual_capabilities: Designs batch and streaming pipeline architectures around volume, latency, consistency, and reliability requirements.
Recommends storage, processing, orchestration, and cloud services for warehouse and lakehouse workloads.
Plans dimensional models, incremental loading, change data capture, partitioning, and query optimization.
Defines data quality checks, lineage, access controls, privacy measures, monitoring, and failure recovery.
Evaluates performance, scalability, operational complexity, and cloud cost tradeoffs.
limitations: It provides guidance and generated artifacts but does not deploy infrastructure or access data systems by itself.
Recommendations require accurate source schemas, workloads, service levels, compliance needs, and platform constraints.
Generated designs and implementation details need environment-specific testing, security review, and cost validation.
It is not intended for standalone exploratory analysis or model development without data pipeline requirements.

use_cases.title: Build an Analytics Warehouse
use_cases.description: Plan ingestion, dbt transformations, dimensional models, tests, lineage, and orchestration for a governed analytics warehouse.

use_cases.title: Design a Streaming Platform
use_cases.description: Select messaging, processing, storage, schema evolution, monitoring, and recovery patterns for low-latency event workloads.

use_cases.title: Modernize Data Governance
use_cases.description: Define quality controls, catalogs, access policies, privacy safeguards, retention rules, and audit processes across data products.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Basic Batch Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend a batch pipeline from [source] to [warehouse]. Use [daily volume], [refresh target], and [cloud]. Explain components, checks, and operations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a scheduled ingestion workflow

prompt_templates.title: Design a Warehouse Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a dimensional model for [business process]. Include grain, facts, dimensions, history handling, incremental loads, tests, lineage, and key assumptions.

prompt_templates.title: Architect a Streaming Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Architect a streaming pipeline for [event source] at [throughput] and [latency]. Address schemas, ordering, duplicates, late data, recovery, monitoring, and cost.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate an Enterprise Data Platform
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [options] for [workload portfolio]. Score scalability, reliability, governance, security, migration effort, operating complexity, and cost. Recommend a phased architecture.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert platform strategy and migration planning

output_examples.input: Design a daily pipeline from PostgreSQL to BigQuery for finance reporting.
output: Architecture: incremental extraction, object storage staging, warehouse loading, dbt transformations, and scheduled orchestration.
Controls: source reconciliation, schema validation, freshness checks, duplicate detection, and protected finance access.
Operations: retries, backfills, lineage, cost monitoring, alert ownership, and recovery procedures.

output_examples.input: Plan a Kafka pipeline for late and out-of-order delivery.
output: Processing plan: event-time windows, watermarks, durable checkpoints, idempotent sinks, and a dead-letter path.
Reliability plan: schema compatibility, replay testing, lag alerts, duplicate metrics, and documented recovery objectives.

output_examples.input: Compare Snowflake and BigQuery for a multi-team analytics platform.
output_examples.output: A structured comparison covering workload fit, scaling, governance, ecosystem integration, administration, migration effort, and cost assumptions, followed by a justified recommendation.

best_practices: Provide data volumes, latency targets, retention, consistency, recovery objectives, and expected growth.
Specify current tools, cloud constraints, source schemas, sink requirements, team skills, and budget limits.
Request quality, security, governance, observability, cost, and failure recovery requirements in every production design.
anti_patterns: Do not request a tool choice without describing workloads, service levels, constraints, and ownership.
Do not deploy generated configurations before testing permissions, data correctness, failure behavior, and rollback procedures.
Do not optimize only for throughput while ignoring quality, privacy, operational complexity, and total cost.

faq.question: Does this skill deploy data infrastructure?
faq.answer: No. It produces architecture and implementation guidance that teams must review, test, and deploy in their own environments.

faq.question: Which data tools can it cover?
faq.answer: It covers common tools for Spark, dbt, Airflow, Kafka, Flink, warehouses, lakehouses, catalogs, quality systems, and cloud data services.

faq.question: Can it design for AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud?
faq.answer: Yes. It can compare and design with data services across all three platforms when requirements and constraints are supplied.

faq.question: What information improves the recommendations?
faq.answer: Provide source types, schemas, volumes, growth, latency, retention, users, compliance needs, reliability targets, existing tools, and budget.

faq.question: Does it address security and governance?
faq.answer: Yes. It can include encryption, least privilege, masking, lineage, catalogs, retention, audit logging, and compliance considerations.

faq.question: Is it suitable for exploratory data analysis?
faq.answer: Not as the primary task. Use it when analysis depends on designing, operating, or improving data pipelines and platforms.
